correctness.rationale: A balanced nonempty word can delete itself, and the empty word loses. For nonzero balance each endpoint deletion preserves the total balance and cuts the itinerary exactly at an interior A (prefix) or B (suffix), leaving that symbol as an endpoint. In the interior game, a Dyck word leaves only nonzero-sum interiors when cut at a legal symbol. In a non-Dyck word, cutting the suffix from the first negative step leaves a Dyck prefix; if there is no negative step, cutting through the last unmatched A leaves a Dyck suffix. Induction applies to the strictly length-decreasing game. Excursions between consecutive visits to {0,h} concatenate uniquely: an exterior return has the primitive Catalan series P, while the interior return and crossing entries follow by cofactors of I-zA on the length-(h-1) path, whose determinant is D_(h-1). For h=1 these reduce to no interior return and a single-step crossing. An interior with j pairs and k peaks contributes k A-to-B changes and k-1 reverse changes; the outer endpoints add two equal-boundary pairs when j>0. This gives the stated Narayana weights and the lone v_h term when j=0. Letter exchange handles negative balance; finite valuation makes all sums coefficientwise valid. On b^i a^j b, j=i+1 is balanced, j<=i produces a first interior B, and j>=i+2 gives itinerary AABB. The slice has infinitely many distinct left residuals, establishing nonregularity.

value.rationale: Counting every losing binary starting word by actual length is a natural complement to the known reduced-game criterion. The itinerary eradicates most original letter positions, so its known Dyck classification does not say how often positions occur. The exact height-resolved factors recover this lost length information and allow computation at every length without solving the complete game tree. Nonregularity also distinguishes this rule from games governed by a finite-state losing language.
residual_risks: The scope is two uniform letter weights and one deletion rule; the formula yields neither asymptotics nor a complete Sprague–Grundy spectrum.
